requirements.requirement: A branch in `config.protectedBranches` (default master, dev) is refused for BOTH remove and merge, and `force:true` does NOT bypass that check.

requirements.requirement: Tests actually prove the attack: tampered index → protected branch refused even with force (nothing deleted/merged), mismatch refused, ghost branch refused, detached refused, valid record still works.
evidence: worktree.test.ts → describe("recorded branch revalidation (N1)") holds exactly those five arms; all 5 pass in the run (41 pass / 0 fail / 165 expect() calls).

findings.title: The new branch-existence gate converts the documented 'missing path is pruned' case into a permanent refusal when the branch is also gone.
findings.where: packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/src/ops.ts → revalidateRecordedBranch: the `if (!branchExists(repo, entry.branch))` throw is placed BEFORE the `if (!pathPresent)` branch.
why_it_matters: The frozen contract .mpd/plans/agent-worktrees.md §3 Lane A says: 'A missing path is pruned, not an error.' The tool description of mpd_worktree_remove in src/index.ts repeats it unconditionally, and all four user-facing docs repeat it (docs/worktree.md, docs/worktree.zh-CN.md, README.md, README.zh-CN.md).

Reachable state: removeWorktree deletes the directory and then the branch before writing the index tombstone (no transaction across git and the index), so a crash between deleteBranch and writeIndex leaves an ACTIVE record with no directory and no branch. External cleanup (`rm -rf` the worktree + `git branch -D`) produces the same state.

Probe section A proves the consequence: remove(force:true) throws `branch-missing`, the record stays `active`, and `createWorktree` for the same name then refuses `name-registered` — the name is unusable through the tool until someone hand-creates the branch or hand-edits the index. Probe section C shows the sibling case: a PRESENT worktree whose branch ref was deleted out of band also refuses `branch-missing` and keeps the directory.
The check adds no protection in the vanished-directory remove path: when the branch does not exist there is nothing for `deleteBranch` to delete, so refusing cannot prevent a deletion.
findings.direction: Move the branch-existence refusal behind the `!pathPresent` branch (apply it only when a live worktree directory exists), or let the vanished-directory remove path prune and report `branchDeleted:false` when the branch is already gone. Keep the protected check ahead of both, since a protected recorded branch must still be refused (R3). Add a test arm for vanished-dir + vanished-branch that asserts a tombstone / `branchDeleted:false` rather than `branch-missing`.

findings.title: The four new doc sentences read as unconditional revalidation; the vanished-directory remove path skips the HEAD comparison.
findings.where: docs/worktree.md, docs/worktree.zh-CN.md, packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/README.md, packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/README.zh-CN.md — the added 'Before either operation uses the recorded branch … revalidate it against the branch git reports' sentences.
findings.why_it_matters: Requirement 6 asks the docs to match the implementation. A reader of the security note is told remove always compares HEAD against the record; for a vanished directory it cannot, and remove proceeds after the name/protection/existence checks. The bound is stated in the function's own comment but nowhere user-facing. Overstating a security check is how a later reader trusts the wrong guarantee.
findings.direction: Add one clause to all four files: a vanished worktree directory cannot answer for HEAD, so remove validates the recorded name, its existence and protection only (and merge refuses); mirror it in the zh-CN twin.

findings.title: The new `invalid-branch` refusal on remove/merge has no test arm.
findings.where: packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/test/worktree.test.ts → describe("recorded branch revalidation (N1)") vs packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/src/ops.ts → revalidateRecordedBranch.
findings.why_it_matters: The isValidBranch guard is the option-injection guard: without it a tampered `entry.branch = "-D"` reaches `git branch -d|-D` as an extra option. Requirement 5's five enumerated arms are all present, so this is not a requirement miss, but the guard is proven only at createWorktree; a regression that removes it at the new call site would keep the suite green. Probe section D shows the behavior itself is correct today (`invalid-branch` for `-D`, `bad..name`, `head~1`, `foo bar`, `HEAD` on both operations).
findings.direction: Add one arm that tampers `entry.branch` to `-D` (and optionally `bad..name`) and asserts `invalid-branch` for both operations plus the survival of the real branch and directory.

declinedToJudge: Merge-TARGET protection remains force-bypassable — pre-existing and frozen in .mpd/plans/agent-worktrees.md §3 Lane A; requirement 3's no-force rule is about the RECORDED branch and is verified. Not changed by this diff.

The original N1 direction also named a refusal for 'the main checkout's HEAD'; no literal check was added. Probed (section G): a record pointing at the main checkout with branch=main passes revalidation, but remove then fails `git-failed` (git refuses to remove the main working tree) and merge is a self-merge no-op returning merged:true with HEAD unmoved — non-destructive, tamper-only, and out of the task's six enumerated requirements.

The vanished-directory remove path still deletes an existing UNPROTECTED branch named by the record (no HEAD to interrogate). This is exactly the task's stated bound; a future hardening could prune-only for vanished directories, but it is not counted as a finding against N1.

A consistent path+branch tamper could point the record at another registered worktree of the same repo and pass all checks. N1 names the branch field; path trust is the pre-existing N6 residual from the PR #111 review. Out of scope here.

Validation is check-then-act (TOCTOU): a member could switch the worktree HEAD between validation and the git call. The destructive operations consume only the validated branch NAME, so a protected branch cannot be redirected into deletion/merge; the directory could be removed while on another branch, which is recoverable and within the stated bound.

`isValidBranch` uses `git check-ref-format --branch` only for its exit code; that mode can expand names like `@{-1}`. Any expansion still fails `branchExists`/the equality check, so the path is fail-closed (probe D/E).

`protectedBranches: []` explicitly disables the list (resolveConfig filters to real strings; only an absent key keeps the default pair). Pre-existing documented config semantics, not changed by this diff.

createForMember still returns an existing active record's `branch` without revalidation. N1 names remove/merge only, the branch is descriptive there, and the cwd is separately gated by existsSync + isGitManaged.
Case-folding of protected branch names (e.g. `MASTER` on a case-insensitive filesystem) was not exercised on this Linux host; no evidence either way, and the equality check would refuse any mismatch.

Merge of a branch whose worktree directory vanished now refuses `unregistered-worktree` (probe section F). This is a deliberate fail-closed choice consistent with R2 (nothing is checked out to interrogate); the task's stated bound names remove only, so it is recorded rather than judged.
